_comment: Candidate-specific packaging manifest for the Frontera runtime. Produced by the P0-PKG-07 follow-up, which closed ten defects found by review after PR #112 merged. It records the identity of a produced artifact and authorizes nothing: no registry publication, no tag, no GitHub Release, no merge. release/RELEASE_MANIFEST.json is a separate machine-generated file and is not this document. Supersedes release/frontera-candidate-manifest-1.1.0.json, which is retained unchanged as the honest record of the superseded artifact and the defects it shipped with.
exports_fingerprint_note: Carried forward unchanged, and verifiably so: the `exports` object in package.json is byte-identical to the object at both the 1.1.0 source commit (74308ad) and the 1.0.0 source commit (11edd06). This release changes the *type* returned by one exported function and adds exported type names, but introduces no subpath and re-targets nothing, so the export map itself is untouched. The standing caveat from 1.1.0 still applies: no script in this repository recomputes this value, so an increment that changes the export map must establish a scripted computation first rather than hand-recording a new number.
license: UNLICENSED (proprietary; LICENSE ships in the tarball)

verification_results.check:clean-room-consumer: PASS (10/10 exports; durable-authority lifecycle proven across separate OS processes)
verification_results.legal:check:strict: PRE-EXISTING FAIL (busboy@1.6.0, streamsearch@1.1.0 carry no recorded license in package-lock.json). Reproduced identically on the unmodified base tree; unrelated to this increment; not part of validate:release or validate:v1-release, so it does not gate this artifact.

reproducibility.method: two git worktrees detached at source_commit, in different directories, each npm ci + npm run build + npm pack; identical bytes

supersedes.status: SUPERSEDED -- merged to main as PR #112, never published, never tagged
supersedes.reason: A post-merge review found ten defects, six reproduced against the merged code. Four contradicted guarantees 1.1.0 asserted in its own documentation: persisted events were not tamper-evident (a capability token's actions and scopes could be widened in place and hydrated as authority); a revocation lost from the end of a chain resurrected the entity as active; the durable evaluation surface exposed mutable Recognition/Authority runtimes, so an application could mint itself credentials and be allowed without an operator context; and an omitted organization was read as an implicit match, which also bypassed organization-scoped API-key authorization. Two more were operational: a legitimately-provisioned grant whose id sorted before its parent's permanently bricked every subsequent hydration, and backup:v1 began demanding the authority database from deployments that had the feature disabled. 1.1.0 must not be consumed downstream.

durable_authority_capability.evaluation_surface: createDurableKernelProviders() -> DurableKernelDecisionService (read-only; carries no Recognition/Authority runtime handles) + AocKernel.evaluate()
durable_authority_capability.api_freeze_impact: none -- the frozen v1 HTTP surface is unchanged (27 endpoints, 34 frozen routes)
durable_authority_capability.restart_durability: PASS (in-process reopen, separate OS processes, and clean-room consumer)
durable_authority_capability.revocation_durability: PASS (same process, after restart, across backup/restore, and against a truncated event tail)
durable_authority_capability.tamper_evidence: PASS (event digests recomputed from their own fields on every read; chain head cross-checked against the independently recorded head)
durable_authority_capability.backup_restore_coverage: included in backup:v1 / restore:v1 / check:portability-smoke when durable authority is enabled; a deployment with the feature disabled is not asked for the database

pmfreak_integration_status: HELD -- the downstream handoff is deliberately not resumed on 1.1.0; this artifact is the candidate for it once reviewed.
